question_text: Archaeologists realised that the boat had been damaged on purpose.
source_reference: Official Guide to IELTS Academic Test 1
passage_text: The seams had been made watertight by pads of moss, fixed by wedges and yew stitches. The timbers that closed the recovered end of the boat had been removed in antiquity when it was abandoned, but much about its original shape could be deduced. There was also evidence for missing upper side planks. The boat was not a wreck, but had been deliberately discarded, dismantled and broken.

metadata.source_pack: Official Guide to IELTS Academic Test 1

question_text: Initially, only the technological aspects of the boat were examined.
source_reference: Official Guide to IELTS Academic Test 1
passage_text: With hindsight, it was significant that the boat was found and studied by mainstream archaeologists who naturally focused on its cultural context. At the time, ancient boats were often considered only from a narrower technological perspective, but news about the Dover boat reached a broad audience. In 2002, on the tenth anniversary of the discovery, the Dover Bronze-Age Boat Trust hosted a conference, where this meeting of different traditions became apparent. Alongside technical papers about the boat, other speakers explored its social and economic contexts, and the religious perceptions of boats in Bronze-Age societies.

question_text: Archaeologists went back to the site to try and find the missing northern end of the boat.
source_reference: Official Guide to IELTS Academic Test 1
passage_text: At the base of a deep shaft six metres below the modern streets a wooden structure was revealed. Cleaning away the waterlogged site overlying the timbers, archaeologists realised its true nature. They had found a prehistoric boat, preserved by the type of sediment in which it was buried. It was then named the Dover Bronze-Age Boat.

metadata.source_pack: Official Guide to IELTS Academic Test 1

question_text: Evidence found in 2004 suggested that the Bronze-Age Boat had been used for trade.
source_reference: Official Guide to IELTS Academic Test 1
